name: verify
description: Prove a change works. verify-feature drives a change through its real surface (CLI, API, UI, library, agent) and captures runtime evidence instead of trusting green tests; verify-this turns "does it work" into a falsifiable claim with baseline and treatment and one of VERIFIED, NOT VERIFIED or INCONCLUSIVE; santa-method gates output behind two independent reviewers who must both pass; control-cli and control-ui build local harnesses for interactive CLIs and for browser or Electron UIs; full-page-screenshot captures a whole page over the Chrome DevTools Protocol with one dependency-free Node script. For QA: dogfood explores a web app and writes a repro-backed issue report, adversarial-ux-test roleplays a hostile user and filters the rant into real tickets, webapp-testing scripts Playwright against local servers it starts for you, ui-demo records polished demo videos, ios-simulator drives the iOS Simulator with 21 accessibility-driven scripts, and windows-desktop-e2e tests WPF, WinForms, Win32 and Qt apps with pywinauto. For test suites: playwright-pro (init, generate from 55 templates, review, fix flaky), react-testing, integration-e2e-testing (lanes, budgets, ROI), bats-testing-patterns, test-audit (retire low-value tests in approved batches) and k6-load-testing. Review lenses: click-path-audit for buttons whose handlers undo each other, api-design-reviewer with an OpenAPI linter, breaking-change detector and scorecard, python-anti-patterns and ai-debt-detector. Contains third-party skills under their own licenses — see NOTICE.md.
